0.title: Create the Discord application
0.body: Open the Discord Developer Portal → New Application → name it “Bow Down Visuals”. Copy the Application ID (General Information) — that's your DISCORD_CLIENT_ID.

1.title: Create the bot user
1.body: Go to Bot → Reset Token → copy the token — that's DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN. No privileged intents needed; leave them off.

2.title: Install the bot on your server
2.body: Click “Install bot on your server” below (or paste your server, channel, and role IDs in the form). You need Manage Server permission.

3.title: Set the environment variables
3.body: On the bot service AND the api-server: DISCORD_CLIENT_ID, DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN (bot only), DISCORD_BOT_SHARED_SECRET (both, 32+ random chars — generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`).

4.title: Run the database migration
4.body: Run lib/db/migrations/0029_discord_bot.sql against production Postgres once, then deploy. The bot announces from your next Go Live.

llcGuide.checklist10Detail: File your annual/biennial report and pay the ongoing state fee on time. Missing them can dissolve your LLC — set a calendar reminder now.
llcGuide.checklist1Detail: For 95% of creators, your home state is the right answer. Filing in Delaware or Wyoming while living elsewhere usually means paying for a foreign LLC registration in your home state too.
llcGuide.checklist2Detail: Search your Secretary of State's business name database. Your LLC name must be unique in that state and usually has to include “LLC” or “Limited Liability Company”.
llcGuide.checklist3Detail: Someone with a physical address in the state who can receive legal mail. You can be your own agent for free (your address becomes public record) or hire a service (~$100–$300/yr).
llcGuide.checklist4Detail: The one document that creates your LLC. File online with the Secretary of State and pay the state filing fee — see the fee table below for your state.
llcGuide.checklist5Detail: Even solo creators should have one — it defines ownership, how money moves, and what happens if you add a partner. Templates work for single-member LLCs.
llcGuide.checklist6Detail: Your federal tax ID. Free directly from IRS.gov — never pay a service for this. You'll need it for the bank account and tax filings.

llcGuide.checklist8Detail: Most creators don't need special licenses, but check your city/county. If you sell merch, you may need a sales tax permit in your state.
llcGuide.checklist9Detail: Track every dollar in and out. A spreadsheet works at first; accounting software pays for itself once brand deals and royalties start flowing.

LLC rules, fees, and tax treatment vary by state and change over time — verify everything with your Secretary of State and consult a licensed business attorney or CPA for your situation.
llcGuide.errAnswer: Couldn't get an answer — try again.
llcGuide.faq1A: Not on day one — but once you're earning real money (brand deals, ad revenue, royalties, merch), an LLC separates your personal assets from business liability and makes you look professional to sponsors. Many creators form one once they cross a few thousand dollars a year in income.
llcGuide.faq1Q: Do I actually need an LLC as a content creator?
llcGuide.faq2A: A sole proprietor IS you — no separation, so a lawsuit or debt can reach your personal assets. An LLC is a separate legal entity: business debts and most lawsuits stop at the company. LLCs also unlock business bank accounts and cleaner taxes as you grow.
llcGuide.faq2Q: LLC vs. sole proprietor — what's the difference?
llcGuide.faq3A: Almost certainly not. If you live and work in your home state, you'll still have to register there as a “foreign LLC” — paying both states' fees. The out-of-state hype mostly benefits the formation companies selling it. File where you live.
llcGuide.faq3Q: Should I file in Delaware, Wyoming, or Nevada instead of my home state?
llcGuide.faq4A: By default the IRS treats a single-member LLC like a sole proprietor: profits flow to your personal tax return (pass-through taxation). No double tax. As income grows, some creators elect S-corp taxation to save on self-employment tax — that's a conversation for a CPA.
llcGuide.faq5A: The state filing fee is the only mandatory cost — $35 to $500 depending on your state (see the table). Add the ongoing annual fee ($0–$800/yr depending on state). An EIN is free from the IRS. Budget services will happily charge you hundreds extra — you don't need them for a standard filing.
llcGuide.faq5Q: How much does it really cost?
llcGuide.faq6A: Yes, in every state. It's free. The tradeoff: your name and address go on public record, and you must be available at that address during business hours to receive legal documents. Many creators start DIY and switch to a service later.
llcGuide.faq6Q: Can I be my own registered agent?
llcGuide.faq7A: Online filings are often approved in days (Colorado can be same-day); mailed filings take weeks. Check the processing column in the fee table for your state.
